verdict.MOBILE_NOT_LINKED.sentence: TODO_TA: Your identity check is not finished, and the phone number on your Aadhaar cannot receive the code.
verdict.MOBILE_NOT_LINKED.why: TODO_TA: PM-KISAN checks who you are before it releases money. The usual way is a one-time code sent to the phone number linked to your Aadhaar. No number is linked to yours, so that code has nowhere to go, and waiting longer will not change it. You need a route that does not use a code: a Common Service Centre can finish the check in person with your Aadhaar card.
verdict.MAPPER_INACTIVE.sentence: TODO_TA: Your bank has not linked your Aadhaar to your account, so the money has nowhere to land.
verdict.MAPPER_INACTIVE.why: TODO_TA: PM-KISAN does not send money to an account number. It sends money to your Aadhaar, and your bank keeps a live link between the two. Yours is switched off, so each instalment is approved and then has nowhere to go. Only your bank branch can switch it back on, and it takes about 7 to 10 working days after they do.
verdict.LAND_NAME_MISMATCH.sentence: TODO_TA: Your land record is in a different name from your Aadhaar, so your state has paused your payment.
verdict.LAND_NAME_MISMATCH.why: TODO_TA: Your state checks that the person claiming the money is the person on the land record. Yours reads {land_name} while your Aadhaar reads {aadhaar_name}. Until those agree the state will not release the instalment. This cannot be fixed online: the village revenue officer has to correct the land record, which usually takes about 30 days.
verdict.FTO_IN_QUEUE.sentence: TODO_TA: Your ₹{amount} has been approved and is on its way. It should reach you by {expected_by}.
verdict.FTO_IN_QUEUE.why: TODO_TA: Nothing is blocking your payment. It has passed every check and is waiting its turn to be paid out. If it has not reached your account by {expected_by}, that is the point to act: come back here and we will tell you which office to take it to.
verdict.PAYMENT_OVERDUE.sentence: TODO_TA: Your ₹{amount} was due by {expected_by}. That was {days_overdue} days ago and it has still not arrived.
verdict.PAYMENT_OVERDUE.why: TODO_TA: Your payment passed every check and was queued for release, so nothing is wrong with your record. A payment this far past its date is stuck, not slow. Take your registration number {reg_no} to your Block Agriculture Officer and ask them to trace it. A payment pending {days_overdue} days is exactly what that office exists to chase.
verdict.ACCOUNT_DORMANT.sentence: TODO_TA: Your bank returned the money because your account has gone dormant.
verdict.ACCOUNT_DORMANT.why: TODO_TA: A bank freezes an account that has had no customer activity for a long time. The money was sent correctly and your bank refused it. Take your passbook and Aadhaar to your branch and ask them to make the account active again. Once it is active the next instalment arrives normally, and you can ask them to re-present the one that came back.
verdict.CREDITED.sentence: TODO_TA: ₹{amount} was paid into your account ending {last4} on {date}.
verdict.CREDITED.why: TODO_TA: This instalment is not missing. It reached your account on {date} and no message was sent to tell you. Ask at your bank counter for a passbook update, or check a mini statement for that date. If your passbook shows nothing on {date}, come back here and we will treat it as a failed payment.
verdict.INCOME_TAX_PAYER.sentence: TODO_TA: Your record is marked as an income tax payer for {year}, which the scheme treats as a reason to stop payment.
verdict.INCOME_TAX_PAYER.why: TODO_TA: PM-KISAN excludes farmers who paid income tax in the last assessment year. This flag is often wrong: it can come from a mistaken match on a similar name or an old tax number. If you did not pay income tax that year, the exclusion can be challenged with your Block Agriculture Officer. There is a second exemption that is missed constantly: Multi-Tasking Staff and Class IV or Group D employees are excluded from the government-service exclusion, so being a government employee in one of those grades does not disqualify you.
verdict.REGISTRATION_REJECTED.sentence: TODO_TA: Your application was not accepted, so no instalment can be paid. The reason recorded is: {reason}.
verdict.REGISTRATION_REJECTED.why: TODO_TA: A rejected application stops payment before any other check matters. Everything else in your record may be correct, and fixing your identity check or your bank link will not release this money while the application stands rejected. Take the recorded reason and your Aadhaar to a Common Service Centre and ask them to correct and resubmit it.
verdict.SYSTEM_UNREACHABLE.sentence: TODO_TA: We could not reach one of the government record systems, so we will not guess at your answer.
verdict.SYSTEM_UNREACHABLE.why: TODO_TA: Seven separate systems have to agree before your money moves, and one of them did not respond. We could show you a likely answer, but a wrong one would send you to the wrong office and cost you a day's wage. Your case is saved on this phone. Try again in a few minutes and we will check the rest for you.
verdict.REGISTRATION_PENDING.sentence: TODO_TA: Your application is still being checked, so no instalment can be paid yet.
verdict.REGISTRATION_PENDING.why: TODO_TA: New applications are checked against your state's land records before any money is released, and payments do not start until that finishes. If it has been more than 30 days since you applied, ask at a Common Service Centre what the current status is.
verdict.GOVT_EMPLOYEE.sentence: TODO_TA: Your record is marked as government service, which the scheme treats as a reason to stop payment.
verdict.GOVT_EMPLOYEE.why: TODO_TA: Serving and retired government employees are excluded from PM-KISAN. Multi-Tasking Staff and Class IV or Group D grades are exempt from that exclusion. If you are in one of those grades, take your service certificate to your Block Agriculture Officer and ask for the exclusion to be lifted.
verdict.PENSIONER.sentence: TODO_TA: Your recorded monthly pension is ₹{pension}, at or above the ₹{threshold} limit for this scheme.
verdict.PENSIONER.why: TODO_TA: Retired government employees drawing ₹{threshold} a month or more are excluded from PM-KISAN. Multi-Tasking Staff and Class IV or Group D grades are exempt. If your pension is lower than the amount recorded here, take your pension order to your Block Agriculture Officer and ask for the record to be corrected.
verdict.LAND_ACQUIRED_AFTER_CUTOFF.sente: TODO_TA: Your land is recorded as acquired on {acquired_on}, after the scheme cut-off of {cutoff}.
verdict.LAND_ACQUIRED_AFTER_CUTOFF.why: TODO_TA: PM-KISAN covers land held on or before {cutoff}. Land recorded as acquired after that date does not qualify. If you held this land earlier and the date of entry is wrong, the village revenue officer can correct it.
verdict.FAMILY_DUPLICATE.sentence: TODO_TA: Another member of your household is already receiving this benefit.
verdict.FAMILY_DUPLICATE.why: TODO_TA: The scheme pays one family once, and counts husband, wife and minor children as a single family. If the other person is not part of your household, take both registration numbers to your Block Agriculture Officer and ask for the records to be separated.
verdict.DOB_MISMATCH.sentence: TODO_TA: Your date of birth reads {on_record} here and {on_aadhaar} on your Aadhaar, so the identity check cannot finish.
verdict.DOB_MISMATCH.why: TODO_TA: The identity check compares your scheme record against Aadhaar field by field and stops if any of them differ. Two digits written the wrong way round is the usual cause. A Common Service Centre can correct the scheme record to match your Aadhaar. Take your Aadhaar card with you.
verdict.GENDER_MISMATCH.sentence: TODO_TA: Your gender is recorded differently here and on your Aadhaar, so the identity check cannot finish.
verdict.GENDER_MISMATCH.why: TODO_TA: The identity check compares your scheme record against Aadhaar field by field and stops if any of them differ. A Common Service Centre can correct the scheme record to match your Aadhaar. Take your Aadhaar card with you.
verdict.NAME_VARIANCE.sentence: TODO_TA: Your name reads {on_record} here and {on_aadhaar} on your Aadhaar, so the identity check cannot finish.
verdict.NAME_VARIANCE.why: TODO_TA: The two spellings have to match before the check will pass. A Common Service Centre can correct the scheme record to match your Aadhaar. Take your Aadhaar card, and ask them to change the scheme record rather than the Aadhaar.
verdict.EKYC_PENDING_ACTION.sentence: TODO_TA: Your identity check is not finished, so no instalment can be paid.
verdict.EKYC_PENDING_ACTION.why: TODO_TA: PM-KISAN checks who you are before releasing money, and yours has not been completed. You can finish it with a one-time code sent to the phone number linked to your Aadhaar, or in person at a Common Service Centre. It takes about 7 to 10 working days to take effect once it is done.
verdict.MAPPER_NOT_FOUND.sentence: TODO_TA: Your Aadhaar is not linked to any bank account, so the money has nowhere to land.
verdict.MAPPER_NOT_FOUND.why: TODO_TA: PM-KISAN pays to your Aadhaar rather than to an account number, and no bank has claimed that link for you. Take your Aadhaar and passbook to your bank branch and ask them to link your Aadhaar to your account. It takes about 7 to 10 working days to take effect.
verdict.MAPPER_DIFFERENT_BANK.sentence: TODO_TA: Your Aadhaar is linked to an account at {other_bank}, so the money is going somewhere you are not looking.
verdict.MAPPER_DIFFERENT_BANK.why: TODO_TA: Money follows the most recent bank that claimed your Aadhaar, and yours points at {other_bank}. Check that account first, because the instalment may already be sitting in it. If you want payments to arrive somewhere else, ask that bank to link your Aadhaar to the account you use.
verdict.LAND_NOT_SEEDED.sentence: TODO_TA: Your land record has not been attached to your application, so your state cannot approve the payment.
verdict.LAND_NOT_SEEDED.why: TODO_TA: Your state releases money only against a land record it can see, and yours is not attached to your application. Take your land document and Aadhaar to the village revenue officer and ask them to attach it. This usually takes about 30 days.
verdict.STATE_HOLD.sentence: TODO_TA: Your state has paused this payment and has not recorded a reason we can read.
verdict.STATE_HOLD.why: TODO_TA: State governments can hold a payment for checks of their own, and the reason is not always published. Your Block Agriculture Officer can see it on their screen. Take your registration number {reg_no} and ask them what the hold is for and what will clear it.
verdict.RFT_SIGNED.sentence: TODO_TA: Your state has approved this payment and passed it on. It should reach you by {expected_by}.
verdict.RFT_SIGNED.why: TODO_TA: Nothing is stuck. Your state has signed off and the payment has moved on to the central system. If it has not arrived by {expected_by}, come back here and we will tell you which office to take it to.
verdict.SETTLEMENT_PENDING.sentence: TODO_TA: The money has been sent and is settling at your bank. It should reach you by {expected_by}.
verdict.SETTLEMENT_PENDING.why: TODO_TA: The payment has left the government system and is with your bank. Banks usually take 1 to 3 working days to post it to your passbook. If nothing has appeared by {expected_by}, ask at your branch counter with your account number.
verdict.NOT_YET_QUEUED.sentence: TODO_TA: Your payment has not been placed in the queue for this instalment yet.
verdict.NOT_YET_QUEUED.why: TODO_TA: Nothing is blocking your record, but this instalment has not yet been picked up for release. It usually clears on its own within the payment cycle. If nothing has changed by {expected_by}, take your registration number {reg_no} to your Block Agriculture Officer.
verdict.BANK_RETURNED.sentence: TODO_TA: Your bank returned the payment, so your account details need correcting.
verdict.BANK_RETURNED.why: TODO_TA: The money was sent and your bank refused it. The usual causes are a wrong account number, a closed account, or a name that does not match the account. Take your passbook and Aadhaar to your branch and ask them why the credit was returned.
verdict.ACCOUNT_CLOSED.sentence: TODO_TA: The account on your record is closed, so your bank sent the money back.
verdict.ACCOUNT_CLOSED.why: TODO_TA: Payments cannot reach a closed account. Open an account or nominate one you already use, then ask that bank to link your Aadhaar to it. Until the link is live the next instalment will come back the same way.
verdict.NONE.sentence: TODO_TA: Nothing is blocking this payment.
verdict.NONE.why: TODO_TA: Every check has passed and no instalment is outstanding for this cycle.

real.row.0.label: TODO_TA: Real
real.row.0.note: TODO_TA: Deterministic rules, fixed B1 to B6 precedence, evidence-carrying. No model involved.
real.row.1.component: TODO_TA: Mock government systems and fault injection
real.row.1.label: TODO_TA: Real
real.row.1.note: TODO_TA: Seven independently modelled, independently failing systems.
real.row.2.component: TODO_TA: Case create, read and event log
real.row.2.label: TODO_TA: Real
real.row.2.note: TODO_TA: Real append-only events. The log lives in server memory only, so it does not survive a restart or reach a second instance.
real.row.3.label: TODO_TA: Not used
real.row.3.note: TODO_TA: No language model runs in this build and none is present in the code. There is no model library, no key is read, and no request leaves the app. Every sentence you see is a pre-authored string in a committed file.
real.row.4.label: TODO_TA: Partly shipped
real.row.4.note: TODO_TA: The selector lists every language the official portal offers. English is the only resolved language; the rest are labelled as coming, and choosing one keeps the interface in English rather than showing you a half-translated screen.
real.row.5.component: TODO_TA: Input checking on our own routes
real.row.5.label: TODO_TA: Hand-written
real.row.5.note: TODO_TA: Our own specification asks for a validation library at the boundary. Adding a dependency the day before submission was judged the larger risk, so inputs are checked by hand. Same coverage, less machinery.
real.row.6.label: TODO_TA: Weaker than specified
real.row.6.note: TODO_TA: A request from another website is refused. A request that sends no Origin header at all - curl, or another server - is served, because inside a single deployment there is no network boundary to enforce. There is a rate limit in the code and it works, but this host starts a fresh instance for almost every request, so the count rarely accumulates: measured on the live site, fourteen rapid requests all succeeded. It would hold on a single-instance deployment, or behind a shared counter this build does not have. What actually protects this is that every field it returns is invented.
real.row.7.label: TODO_TA: Simulated
real.row.7.note: TODO_TA: No real identity system is contacted.
real.row.8.component: TODO_TA: Payment, bank, land record and tax systems
real.row.8.label: TODO_TA: Simulated
real.row.8.note: TODO_TA: Synthetic modules with deliberately inconsistent records and injectable faults.
real.row.9.label: TODO_TA: Simulated
real.row.9.note: TODO_TA: No message is sent to any phone. The demo code is shown on the screen that asks for it.
real.row.10.label: TODO_TA: Synthetic
real.row.10.note: TODO_TA: Eight invented people. Every identifier is structurally invalid as a real credential, so nothing here could be mistaken for or reused as real.
real.row.11.label: TODO_TA: Real, on your device
real.row.11.note: TODO_TA: Kept in this browser. It survives a reload and never leaves your phone.
real.row.12.component: TODO_TA: Offline queue and background sync
real.row.12.label: TODO_TA: Not built
real.row.12.note: TODO_TA: There is still no service worker and no replay queue, so nothing is re-sent for you after a disconnection. What does survive is more than it was: fix-path progress, a filed complaint and every action you complete are all written to this browser before any network attempt, so a lost connection cannot lose them and a second press cannot duplicate them.
real.row.13.component: TODO_TA: Complaint filing, deadline clocks, escalation
real.row.13.label: TODO_TA: Real, with one difference
real.row.13.note: TODO_TA: Filing is real, the deadline is real, and the escalation ladder is real: 15 days to your block officer, then the state officer, then the PM-KISAN Division, with the appeal opening at 30 days. The one difference from our specification is how escalation happens. It describes an hourly job that promotes overdue complaints; there is no such job here, so the same rows are worked out when the page is read. Because every row carries a fixed key, reading a hundred times builds the same list a scheduler would have, not a hundred rows.
real.row.14.label: TODO_TA: Real
real.row.14.note: TODO_TA: Every line on the timeline is an event recorded when it happened, in the same list an officer auditing the case would read. Nothing on that screen is written for the screen.
real.row.15.label: TODO_TA: Available
real.row.15.note: TODO_TA: Read aloud is available through your browser or device's built-in speech synthesis. Voice input through Bhashini is not enabled.
real.row.16.label: TODO_TA: Planned
real.row.16.note: TODO_TA: The microphone button is visible and disabled. It requests no permission and loads no speech library.
real.row.17.label: TODO_TA: Real camera, simulated check
real.row.17.note: TODO_TA: The camera is real: a real browser permission prompt, your own video, real instructions to follow. The verification is simulated - no real Aadhaar system is contacted and the result comes from our mock records. The picture is drawn to a canvas in memory, checked, and discarded in the same step. It is never uploaded and never stored, and our own security policy sends connect-src 'self', so your browser would refuse an upload even if this page tried one. You can check that header in your browser's developer tools.

faq.title: TODO_TA: Common questions
faq.standfirst: TODO_TA: The ten things people most often need answered, in plain language. Tap a question to open it.
faq.still_stuck_body: TODO_TA: If your question is about your own payment, we can check the actual records rather than answer in general.
faq.0.q: TODO_TA: What is e-KYC, and why does it stop my payment?
faq.0.a: TODO_TA: e-KYC is the scheme confirming that you are the person on the record. Until it is finished, no instalment is released, however correct everything else may be. You can complete it with a one-time code sent to the phone number linked to your Aadhaar, or in person at a Common Service Centre using your fingerprint. It takes about 7 to 10 working days to take effect once done.
faq.1.q: TODO_TA: My instalment has not arrived. What do I do first?
faq.1.a: TODO_TA: Do not start by visiting an office. Seven separate government systems have to agree before money moves, and the reason yours stopped sits in exactly one of them. Check your payment here first: you will get the one cause, the one office that can fix it, and what to carry. Going to the wrong counter costs a day's wage and a bus fare.
faq.2.q: TODO_TA: The website says my Aadhaar is not linked to my bank account. What does that mean?
faq.2.a: TODO_TA: The scheme does not send money to an account number. It sends money to your Aadhaar, and your bank keeps a live link between the two. If that link is switched off or was never made, every instalment is approved and then has nowhere to land. Only your bank branch can set it up, and only the branch where you hold the account. It takes about 7 to 10 working days.
faq.3.q: TODO_TA: My land record is in my father's or husband's name. Does that block me?
faq.3.a: TODO_TA: Yes. Your state checks that the person claiming the money is the person on the land record, and pauses the payment when they differ. This is the single most common reason a state holds an instalment, and it cannot be fixed online. The village revenue officer has to correct the record, which usually takes about 30 days.
faq.4.q: TODO_TA: Who is eligible for PM-KISAN?
faq.4.a: TODO_TA: Landholding farmer families, where family means husband, wife and minor children owning cultivable land. The scheme pays one family once, not once per adult. Tenant farmers who do not own the land are not covered. Eligibility is decided by your State or Union Territory government against its own land records, not by the central department.
faq.5.q: TODO_TA: Why would someone be excluded even though they farm?
faq.5.a: TODO_TA: The scheme excludes higher-income categories: institutional landholders, people holding or having held constitutional posts, serving and retired government employees, retired pensioners drawing ten thousand rupees a month or more, income tax payers in the last assessment year, and professionals such as doctors, engineers and lawyers. There is one exemption that is missed constantly: Multi-Tasking Staff and Class IV or Group D employees are excluded from the government-service rule, so being a government employee in one of those grades does not disqualify you.
faq.6.q: TODO_TA: How do I know whether my application was accepted?
faq.6.a: TODO_TA: A rejected application stops payment before any other check matters, and fixing your identity check or bank link will not release money while it stands rejected. Check your status here and we will tell you whether your application was accepted, rejected with a recorded reason, or still being checked.
faq.7.q: TODO_TA: The phone number on my record is one I no longer use. What can I do?
faq.7.a: TODO_TA: This is the dead end that stops most people. The one-time code goes to the number linked to your Aadhaar, so if that phone is gone the code will never arrive and waiting will not help. You have two ways through. Finish the identity check in person at a Common Service Centre with your fingerprint, which needs no code at all. Or take your Aadhaar and your current phone to a Common Service Centre and have the new number linked first.
faq.8.q: TODO_TA: How do I see whether my village list includes me?
faq.8.a: TODO_TA: The official website publishes a beneficiary list by state, district, block and village. It is useful for confirming that your household appears at all. It will not tell you why a payment stopped, because the list only shows who is registered, not what happened to a particular instalment.
faq.9.q: TODO_TA: I want to complain. Where does it actually go?
faq.9.a: TODO_TA: It depends on the problem, and sending it to the wrong place is why complaints stall. The central helpline cannot fix a land record or a state-level hold, because it has no access to your state's records. Land and eligibility problems go to your village revenue officer or Block Agriculture Officer. Bank problems go to your branch. A complaint that names the instalment, the date it was released, the exact status shown, and your registration number resolves faster, because the officer does not have to come back and ask.

act.office_only: TODO_TA: There is nothing on this blocker that can be finished from a phone. That is not us giving up - the change has to be made by an office, so the useful thing we can do is tell you exactly which one, what to carry and what to say.

act.back: TODO_TA: Back to what to do
act.ruled_out.not_this_blocker: TODO_TA: This would not change anything for your case. What is stopping your payment is something else.
act.ruled_out.different_person: TODO_TA: The two names are not two spellings of one name - they are two different people. Confirming a spelling cannot fix that, and only the revenue office can change who a land record belongs to.
act.ruled_out.no_names: TODO_TA: We do not hold both names, so there is nothing to compare.
act.ruled_out.no_account: TODO_TA: We do not have an account number on your record to link.
act.ekyc.title: TODO_TA: Finish your identity check with your camera
act.ekyc.body: TODO_TA: Your identity check needs proof that you are you. The usual way is a code to your phone, and that cannot reach you. Your camera can do it instead, here, in about a minute.
act.ekyc.disclosure: TODO_TA: This is a simulated identity check. No real Aadhaar system is contacted. Your camera picture is used on this device only, is never sent anywhere, and is thrown away the moment the check finishes.
act.ekyc.done: TODO_TA: Your identity check is recorded as complete.
act.ekyc.permission: TODO_TA: Your browser will ask permission to use the camera. Nothing is recorded until you allow it.
act.ekyc.denied: TODO_TA: Your camera is not available, or permission was refused. Nothing is lost - the steps below still work, and a Common Service Centre can finish the same check with your fingerprint.
act.ekyc.step_center: TODO_TA: Look straight at the camera
act.ekyc.step_turn: TODO_TA: Now turn your head slowly to the left
act.ekyc.confirm: TODO_TA: That is enough. Finish the check
act.ekyc.cancel: TODO_TA: Stop and turn the camera off
act.ekyc.live_note: TODO_TA: Nothing is being uploaded. What you see is coming from your camera and going nowhere else.
act.mobile.title: TODO_TA: Change the phone number on your record
act.mobile.body: TODO_TA: The number on your record is one you no longer use, which is why the code never arrives. Give us the number you use now and every future code will reach you.
act.mobile.disclosure: TODO_TA: This is a simulated change. No real Aadhaar or PM-KISAN record is updated, and no message is sent to any phone.
act.mobile.done: TODO_TA: Your new number is recorded.
act.mobile.label: TODO_TA: The phone number you use now
act.mobile.hint: TODO_TA: Ten digits. In this demo any number starting with 5 is accepted, because a real number is not allowed here.
act.mobile.invalid: TODO_TA: That is not a number this demo will accept. Use ten digits starting with 5 - real numbers are deliberately refused so nobody enters one.

act.name.disclosure: TODO_TA: This is a simulated correction. No real land or Aadhaar record is changed.
act.name.done: TODO_TA: Your spelling is recorded, and the correction is on its way to the records that disagree.
act.name.on_aadhaar: TODO_TA: As spelled on your Aadhaar
act.name.on_land: TODO_TA: As spelled on the other record

services.tier_portal: TODO_TA: These belong on the official site
services.tier_portal_note: TODO_TA: Each of these submits something into a government system we have no sanctioned way to write to. A form here that looked real and went nowhere would be worse than a link.

svc.17.name: TODO_TA: Finish your e-KYC
svc.17.body: TODO_TA: The identity check the scheme makes mandatory before it will pay you.
svc.17.reason: TODO_TA: The official route sends a code to the phone number on your Aadhaar. When that number is one you no longer use, the code cannot reach you and the site offers an app download or a trip to a Common Service Centre. Your camera needs no phone number, so we finish it here.
svc.18.name: TODO_TA: Link your Aadhaar to your bank account again
svc.18.body: TODO_TA: The link that lets government payments reach your account.
svc.18.reason: TODO_TA: The official answer is to visit the branch where you hold the account. The request that fixes it is four lines long and needs nothing from you that we do not already hold, so we send it from here.
svc.19.name: TODO_TA: Correct a spelling of your name
svc.19.body: TODO_TA: When two government records spell your name differently.
svc.19.reason: TODO_TA: Two spellings of one name is something you can settle yourself, and we let you. Two different people on a record is not, and we say so and send you to the revenue office rather than offering a form that would achieve nothing.
svc.0.reason: TODO_TA: The official site shows a status string and stops. We read seven records, name the one thing stopping the payment, and tell you who can clear it, what to carry and how long it takes.
svc.1.reason: TODO_TA: The official page tells you the application was rejected. It does not tell you the reason it recorded, which is the only part you can act on. We show that.
svc.2.reason: TODO_TA: The official directory lists offices by district. It does not know your problem, so it cannot tell you which one to go to. Ours names the office for your blocker, what to carry, and what to say when you get there.
svc.6.reason: TODO_TA: The official flow needs you to already be able to receive a code, which is exactly what fails when your number is out of date. We change it without needing the old number to work.
svc.7.reason: TODO_TA: The list answers whether you are on it. It does not answer why your money did not arrive, which is the question people open it to answer. We answer that directly instead.
svc.13.reason: TODO_TA: The official form is an empty box. A complaint naming the instalment, the release date, the exact status string and your registration number is answered faster, and you cannot write that because you cannot read the status page. We write it for you and start a clock on it.
svc.14.reason: TODO_TA: The official answers are written about the scheme. Ours are written about the questions people actually arrive with.
svc.3.reason: TODO_TA: Registering creates a new beneficiary record and requires your state to verify your land records. There is no sanctioned way for us to write into that system, and a form that looked real and submitted nothing would be the worst thing we could build.
svc.4.reason: TODO_TA: Editing a submitted application writes into the scheme's own record. Same reason as registering: we can read a record, we cannot change one.
svc.5.reason: TODO_TA: Supplying a missing detail writes into the scheme record. We can tell you which detail is missing and why it matters, which is the part the official flow does not do.
svc.12.reason: TODO_TA: Moving a record between states needs both states to act. That is a process, not a form, and it is not one a layer over the top can carry out.
svc.15.reason: TODO_TA: This is the app download the identity check pushes you towards. We built the in-browser route precisely so you would not need it, so pointing you at it would undo the point.
svc.16.reason: TODO_TA: The Kisan Credit Card is a different scheme with its own eligibility and its own forms. It sits next to PM-KISAN on the official site; it is not part of this problem.
svc.8.reason: TODO_TA: Refund is the inverse problem: money you received and must return. Different journey, different design, different reader. Answering one problem properly is worth more than answering two badly.
svc.9.reason: TODO_TA: Surrendering a benefit is a decision to stop being paid. Our whole product is for someone who should be paid and is not, so the surrender flows are the opposite direction and are out of scope by choice.
svc.10.reason: TODO_TA: Cancelling a surrender belongs to the same inverse journey. Out of scope for the same reason.
svc.11.reason: TODO_TA: Checking a surrender revocation belongs to the same inverse journey. Out of scope for the same reason.

real.row.19.component: TODO_TA: Where a filed complaint lives
real.row.19.label: TODO_TA: On your device
real.row.19.note: TODO_TA: The date you filed is kept in this browser, not on our server. That is not laziness: this host starts a fresh copy of the app for almost every request, which is the same behaviour that stops our rate limit working, and a filing held only on the server would vanish between two page loads. For a feature whose whole subject is a thirty-day wait, that would be worse than not building it. The cost is that clearing your browser data clears the filing, and it does not follow you to another phone.
real.row.20.label: TODO_TA: On your device
real.row.20.note: TODO_TA: Same as the filing above, for the same reason. The server records that an action happened so the audit trail is real while that copy of the app is alive, but the record you can rely on is the one in this browser.
real.row.21.label: TODO_TA: Real form, simulated change
real.row.21.note: TODO_TA: The form, the checking and the entry on your timeline are real. Nothing is written to any Aadhaar or PM-KISAN record, and no message is sent to any phone. The number you type is not stored on our side at all - we record that you did it, not what you entered.
real.row.22.component: TODO_TA: Ask your bank to link your Aadhaar again
real.row.22.label: TODO_TA: Real request, simulated sending
real.row.22.note: TODO_TA: The request is generated from your own record and is the same wording the printed slip carries to a bank counter. No real bank and no real payment system is contacted.
real.row.23.component: TODO_TA: Correct a spelling of your name
real.row.23.label: TODO_TA: Real, and mostly ruled out
real.row.23.note: TODO_TA: The action works, and for most of our made-up people it refuses to run - which is the honest outcome rather than a fault. It only offers itself when two records hold two spellings of one name. When they hold two different people, as they do for our land-record case, it says so and sends you to the revenue office instead of giving you a form that would change nothing.
real.row.24.component: TODO_TA: What the demo people can show you
real.row.24.label: TODO_TA: One gap, stated
real.row.24.note: TODO_TA: Every land-record mismatch we invented is a genuine one - two different people, not two spellings - because that is the case worth showing. The consequence is that the name-correction action has no demo person who can complete it: on all eight it only ever shows why it cannot help. The action is real and the rule behind it is the same rule the diagnosis uses. We would rather tell you that than invent a ninth person so a button had somewhere to lead.
